Main.sentence: Roseland is one of the 77 official ___E:community areas of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_areas_of_Chicago)___ , ___E:Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois)___ , on the far south side of the city. It includes the ___E:neighborhoods U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighborhoods)___ of Fernwood, Princeton Park, Lilydale, the southern portion of West Chesterfield, Rosemoor, Sheldon Heights and West Roseland.

Roseland was settled in the 1840s by ___E:Dutch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands)___ immigrants, who called the area "de Hooge Prairie", the High Prairie , because it was built on higher, drier ground than the earlier Dutch settlement several miles further south of the ___E:Little Calumet River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Calumet_River)___ , which was called "de Laage Prairie", the Low Prairie , now ___E:South Holland, Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Holland,_Illinois)___ .

The community was entirely agrarian until the late 19th century, when the town of ___E:Pullman, Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman,_Chicago)___ was built between Roseland and ___E:Lake Calumet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Calumet)___ . ___E:George M. Pullman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_M._Pullman)___ planned a model industrial city built around a factory that manufactured his "Palace" railway coaches.
Modern brick homes were built with electricity, plumbing and gas utilities.
Skilled tradesmen from all over Europe immigrated to the town of Pullman with many settling in nearby Roseland.
The Pullman Freight Car Works was built in the 1900s decade on 103rd Street, and survives to this day as a distribution center for flat-rolled steel.
Roseland was annexed into Chicago in 1892. The Roseland area became a very cosmopolitan community made up of multi cultural, ethnic and racial backgrounds.

There was a large population of ___E:Italian Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_American)___ just east of Roseland in the ___E:Kensington community U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kensington,_Illinois&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .

While some Italians of southern Italian origins came to the area from the Little Italy neighborhood on Taylor Street, many other Italians who settled in the area came from the northern Italian regions of Piedmont, Tuscany, and the Veneto.

All these Italians from varied regions of Italy helped to make the Kensington area, and the wider Roseland area, centers of South Side Italian life. Sant' Antonio di Padua (St. Anthony's) Church (built 1903) and its grammar school were key religious and cultural landmarks of the area. Supporting businesses flourished rapidly changing the farmland into commercial and residential communities surrounded by a number of industries.
Stores on Michigan Avenue served the entire south side of Chicago.
Fortunes began to change in the 1960s when industry patterns led to economic decline.
Steel mills to the east were shuttered.

Pullman scaled back production and eventually closed for good in 1981. The huge ___E:Sherwin-Williams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherwin-Williams)___ paint factory closed for good in 1995. A period of rapid ethnic succession took place.

The much lauded ___E:mural U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mural)___ ___E:"I Welcome Myself to a New Place: Roseland Pullman Mural," U:(http://magazine.uchicago.edu/9606/9606Murals2.html)___ by Olivia Gude, Jon Pounds, and Marcus Jefferson, 1988, was designed to unite the predominantly African American community of Roseland with its nearest neighbor, the predominantly white Pullman community.
Fernwood lies on the western edge of Roseland, between 99th and 103rd Streets.

It was considered an "upscale" [citation needed] neighborhood of Roseland and extended west into the ___E:Washington Heights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Heights,_Chicago)___ community up to Halsted Street.
Sometimes referred to as West Roseland, it was incorporated in 1883. The area was known for a gardenlike parkway between 95th and 103rd Streets along Eggelston that was known as Fernwood Parkway.
The area is noted for one of the worst ___E:race riots U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_riots)___ in Chicago history.
In mid August 1947, several black veterans and their families moved into the CHA Fernwood Park Housing Project at 104th and Halsted.
Area residents viewed this as one of several attempts by the ___E:CHA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Housing_Authority)___ to initiate racial integration into white communities.
A violent mob action resulted which lasted for three days and mobilized over 1,000 law enforcement officers to control.

During the 1950s and 1960s the community witnessed the combined effects of ___E:blockbusting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockbusting)___ by unscrupulous real estate agents and the ensuing ___E:white flight U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_flight)___ resulting in complete ethnic transition.
Like the surrounding communities of Roseland and Washington Heights, Fernwood Park remains predominantly African-American.
Lilydale is a small enclave of modest homes in the northwest corner of Roseland.
In the 1920s and 1930s the thinly populated area was referred to as little more than a "cabbage patch".

It consisted of mostly vacant land between 91st and 95th Streets and between State Street and the ___E:Chicago & Eastern Illinois Railroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_%26_Eastern_Illinois_Railroad)___ tracks (then, the ___E:Chicago and Western Indiana Railroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_and_Western_Indiana_Railroad)___ ).

The 1940s saw a peak in the ___E:Second Migration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Migration_(African_American))___ of Black workers from the South seeking jobs and a better life in the industrialized North.
Affordable housing for Blacks was limited and generally restricted to the ___E:"Black Belt" U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Belt_(Chicago))___ on the south side of Chicago.
Housing shortages grew more severe with the onset of ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ as defense workers moved into the city to aid the war effort.
Lilydale became an attractive area due to its proximity to the steel mills and other defense industries on the south side. It was centrally located and convenient to railroads and streetcars.
Beginning in 1942, Black contractors Matthew Goodwin and "Duke" Hodges began building simple, low cost single family homes and duplexes for a growing working-class black neighborhood.
To Black trades workers, Lilydale represented an all-too-rare opportunity to use their skills and help resolve their own housing problem.
While the homes were modest, they were made of brick and many still stand today.

They were originally intended to be rented to defense workers and sold to veterans after the War. The homes were dramatically more affordable than similar homes in the area making them attractive to workers and veterans alike.
Today, only about 12 city blocks remain of the original settlement and the area is generally referred to as a part of Princeton Park.
Princeton Park is a community of single-family homes built in 1944 and is located in the northwest corner of the Roseland community area in ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ .
Originally, it was a subdivision of low cost multi-family row houses between 91st and 95th streets and Wentworth and Harvard streets.
The eastern boundary later extended to State Street (now the Dan Ryan Expressway).
This area includes single-family homes, classic bungalows, that were part of the ___E:Lilydale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilydale,_Chicago)___ community.
The project was the creation of banker/real estate developer Donald O'Toole.

The land had previously been used for farming by the primarily Dutch settlers in the Roseland area. In the early 1900s, Roseland transitioned from a farming community to an urban residential neighborhood.
As one of the last remaining open spaces it was primed for development.
The low cost housing was marketed exclusively to the African-American community making it the first established black community in Roseland.
It remains a segregated African-American community today.
Once established, Princeton Park was on the leading edge of the ensuing "panic peddling" that engulfed Roseland.

Unscrupulous realtors used scare tactics such as ___E:blockbusting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockbusting)___ to frighten and intimidate white residents; churning the real estate market for quick profits.
As suburban housing and commuting became more accessible in the 1960s and 1970s, middle class whites left the Roseland area resulting in a total ethnic transformation.
Roseland is a stronghold for the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ .

In the ___E:2016 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Illinois,_2016)___ , Roseland cast 20,042 votes for ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ and cast 316 votes for ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ .

In the ___E:2012 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Illinois,_2012)___ , Roseland cast 24,400 votes for ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ and cast 132 votes for ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ .
Train service in the community area is provided by ___E:Metra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra)___ .

The ___E:Metra Electric District's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra_Electric_District)___ Main Line runs along the Roseland community area's border with the ___E:Pullman community area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman,_Chicago)___ with stations at ___E:95th Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/95th_Street/Chicago_State_University_station)___ , ___E:103rd Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/103rd_Street_(Rosemoor)_station)___ , ___E:107th Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/107th_Street_station)___ , ___E:111th Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/111th_Street_(Pullman)_station)___ , and ___E:115th Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kensington/115th_Street_station)___ .

The ___E:95th/Dan Ryan station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/95th/Dan_Ryan_station)___ , a terminal station of the ___E:Chicago "L" Red Line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Line_(CTA))___ , is located in Roseland. ___E:Red Ahead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Ahead)___ , a program to extend the Red Line south to 130th Street, would result in new stations in Roseland at 103rd Street and 111th Street.
In 2025, it was estimated that this project will begin construction in 2026 and will be completed in 2030.
___E:Chicago Public Schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Public_Schools)___ operates public schools in Roseland.
K-8 schools in Roseland and serving sections of Roseland include Bennett, Cullen, Curtis, Scanlon, Dunne, Frank L. Gillespie, Alex Haley Academy, L. Hughes, Kohn, and Lavizzo.
K-8 Schools outside of Roseland and serving sections of Roseland include Evers, Fernwood, Pullman, Ryder, and Smith.

Three high schools, ___E:Fenger High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenger_Academy_High_School_(Chicago))___ , ___E:Gwendolyn Brooks College Preparatory Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwendolyn_Brooks_College_Preparatory_Academy)___ and ___E:Harlan Community Academy High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlan_Community_Academy_High_School)___ , are located in Roseland and serve Roseland.

Some Roseland residents are zoned to ___E:Corliss High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corliss_High_School)___ in ___E:Pullman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman,_Chicago)___ , while others are zoned to ___E:Julian High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_High_School_(Chicago))___ in ___E:Washington Heights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Heights,_Chicago)___ .
Chicago Collegiate Charter School, opened in 2013, serves students in Roseland.

Harlan Academic Center and Turner-Drew, K-8 magnets, are in Roseland.  ___E:Gwendolyn Brooks College Preparatory Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwendolyn_Brooks_College_Preparatory_Academy)___ , a magnet school, is located in Roseland.
___E:Roseland Christian School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseland_Christian_School)___ , a private school, is in Roseland.

The main campus of ___E:Chicago State University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_State_University)___ at 95th and ___E:Martin Luther King Drive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Drive_(Chicago))___ , is in the northeast portion of Roseland.
Roseland is one of the deadliest neighborhoods in Chicago, despite stepped-up efforts by City Hall to curb gang violence.
Roseland had 26 shooting deaths in 2021, an increase from the previous year according to Chicago Sun-Times data.
